title: Scoped telemetry vault and policy-led provenance ledger
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a policy-driven telemetry vault that centralizes PII-sensitive observability artifacts (traces, logs, tag-enriched metrics), enforces tenant-aware TTLs, and records an immutable provenance ledger for just-in-time revelation and audit.

Scope:
- Tracing hooks: add lightweight provenance headers and sensitivity tags at span creation points; provide SDK helpers to mark fields as ephemeral vs persistent.
- Metrics/log pipeline: extend the ingest pipeline to honor sensitivity tags, apply tenant-specific retention/TTL, and route redaction transforms before long-term storage.
- Dashboards/access: integrate RBAC checks and an access-audit trail that records who requested 'unmasked' views and why (justification token).

Non-goals: full data classification ML (we will rely on developer annotations + deterministic classifiers as v1). No heavy-weight on-disk encryption changes in this ticket (KMS integration tracked separately).

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Policy model: use a JSON policy bundle evaluated at ingestion that supports (tenant, dataset, sensitivity_level) -> {redaction, ttl_seconds, reveal_policy}. This avoids hard-coded rules in pipelines and enables fast policy rollouts.
- Just-in-time reveal: implement ephemeral reveal tokens tied to an access ledger entry instead of permanently unmasking data. Pros: better auditability and smaller blast radius. Cons: adds latency to ad-hoc investigation workflows; mitigated with a cache for approved investigator tokens.
- Redaction approach: deterministic field-level masking for structured traces, regex + tokenization for logs. For unstructured or ambiguous payloads we mark as "high sensitivity" and degrade retention to the most restrictive tier.
- Performance: Pipeline filters run in the fast path using WASM transforms (to keep CPU cost low) and fall back to worker processes for heavy NLP classification.

Implementation plan:
1) Tracing SDK updates: add tag API and provenance header (ENG-100601; SDK PR linked in comments).
2) Ingest pipeline: implement policy evaluator, TTL annotator, and redaction WASM module (this ticket).
3) Access ledger: append-only ledger service for reveal requests + short-lived reveal tokens.
4) Console integration: dashboard controls for retention overrides, access audit UI, and canned reports.
5) Rollout: feature-flagged in staging -> pilot with two internal teams -> gradual tenant rollout.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Keep additional tail-latency on ingest path < 10ms p50 and < 40ms p99 for the redaction step.
- Alert on policy-eval failures or denied reveals > 0.5% of requests.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Scoped+Telemetry+Vault+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/12345
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/obs-vault-mocks

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK emits sensitivity tags and provenance header (unit+integration tests).
- Ingest pipeline honors TTL and applies redaction for three canonical scenarios (trace span with email, log line with credit-card-like token, metric labels with user_id).
- Reveal workflow produces an access ledger entry and a time-limited reveal token; token-lifetime configurable.
- Console shows access audit entries and allows approved users to request reveals with reason codes.
